newsitem.title: UK: ATHLETICS-CAPOBIANCO UPSET BY FOUR-YEAR BAN OVER DOPE TEST.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-CAPOBIANCO UPSET BY FOUR-YEAR BAN OVER DOPE TEST.

text.p: Australian sprinter Dean Capobianco said on Monday he was staggered by a decision to ban him from athletics for four years for an alleged doping offence.

"We were gobsmacked by the decision. It still hasn't really sunk in yet but I just think it's disgraceful," Capobianco said at London's Heathrow airport after flying in from Monte Carlo where the International Amateur Athletic Federation (IAAF) announced the ban earlier on Monday.
The IAAF said Capobianco had tested positive for the anabolic steroid stanozolol at a meeting in the Netherlands last May.
Capobianco said he believed the test was flawed.
"I still don't believe to this day that it was my sample. I don't think my sample was positive," he said.
The 26-year-old sprinter escaped an automatic four-year ban when the Australian governing body cleared him on the grounds that the testing procedures had been seriously flawed.
The IAAF opposed the Australian decision but allowed Capobianco to compete at last year's Atlanta Olympics after their legal advisors said the federation could be sued successfully in a civil court.
Capobianco was eliminated in the second round of the 200 metres in Atlanta.
The Australian said at Heathrow that the IAAF had given no explanation for the ban, which will keep him out of official competition until only months before the 2000 Sydney Olympics.
"There were no reasons," he said. "I was denied the right to prove my innocence, that is clear. It's totally a political decision and that is the hardest thing to take."
Capobianco said he would apply to the IAAF to have the ban overturned.
"At the moment I can't run and that's been by bread and butter for the last eight years," he said.
"I was confident of winning the case right up until this morning. But what do you do against a body that is as powerful as the IAAF? As an athlete you feel kind of helpless."
